article.title: Acusativo neutro = nominativo
article.chapter: Nominativo y cópula cero en presente — Именительный падеж и нулевая связка

claims.summary: In Russian, the accusative singular of neuter nouns usually has the same form as the nominative singular.
The nominative case is used with the subject of a sentence, while the accusative case can appear with a direct object. In neuter singular nouns, both forms typically coincide.
Examples are provided to illustrate the usage of nominative and accusative cases in Russian, specifically for neuter singular nouns.

links.notes: The article states that the accusative singular of neuter nouns in Russian often coincides with the nominative singular form. This claim is supported by the Wiktionary entry for 'окно', which provides examples of this phenomenon.
